risks.title: Cyberattacks and data breaches
risks.score_rationale: Risk is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of Item 1A with strong language (exposed, protection and dense). Governance is developed, underscoring the importance of this risk. Cybersecurity category weighted at 4/5 in severity.

risks.title: Helms-Burton litigation regarding Cuba
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Item 3 with final judgment of 112M$, appeal pending before Supreme Court (Oct. 2025). Very strong language (significant uncertainties, potentially adverse impact). Existential risk in case of final defeat.

risks.title: Risks related to maritime operations
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly detailed, maritime operations involve intrinsic risks (shipwreck, health, safety). The cruise sector is exposed to major events that can cause large-scale losses. Recurring context in the sector.

risks.title: Increased competition in tourism
risks.score_rationale: The cruise sector is highly competitive. Although not mentioned here, this is a structural risk in the cyclical consumer sector. Implicit position reflected in fleet modernization strategies.

risks.title: Future capital-intensive financial commitments
risks.score_rationale: References in Item 7 regarding ships under construction and financing needs indicate massive investments. Risk of overcapacity or financial distress in case of cycle downturn.

ai_positioning.summary: RCL does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report. Information provided focuses primarily on financial aspects, operations and risks associated with its cruise business.
